prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1176; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of a rear-end collision at a city intersection. Insured vehicle was stopped at a red signal when struck from behind. Police report requested. No injuries reported at scene by either party. Initial liability appears clear in favor of insured's position pending review of photos and statements.

Entry 2: Claimant contacted our office through counsel. Attorney letter of representation received and logged. All further communication to be routed through counsel. Claimant reportedly experienced lower back strain and has been seeing a treating physician. Requested medical records and billing authorization forms sent to counsel's office.

Entry 3: Reviewed scene photos and vehicle damage estimate from the repair shop. Rear bumper, trunk lid, and tail light assembly damaged on the claimant's vehicle. Damage consistent with reported impact. Adjuster noted that the claimant's vehicle has prior unrelated body repair history, which is being reviewed against current estimate.

Entry 4: Medical records received from treating provider through counsel. Diagnosis listed as lumbar strain with recommended physical therapy over several weeks. No imaging-confirmed structural injury noted in the file. Records forwarded to medical review for assessment of treatment duration and relationship to the accident.

Entry 5: Status call with claimant's attorney. Counsel indicated treatment is ongoing and requested evaluation of a settlement demand, which is expected in writing. Reserves reviewed and maintained at current level. File diary set to follow up upon receipt of demand package and completion of medical review.
